value:
`savedregs.py` READS THE POSTPROCESSED OBJECT BY DEFAULT, SO ON A WEBFRANK-PINNED FUNCTION ITS DEFAULT VERDICT IS `ASSIGNMENT MATCHES` BY CONSTRUCTION, AND IT PRINTS NO PIN WARNING TO SAY SO. This is the savedregs instance of the fndiff hazard AGENTS.md already records ('fndiff scores the POSTPROCESSED object, so every webfrank-pinned function reads real 0 by construction'), and it is worse in one specific way: fndiff's answer is a NUMBER a reader knows to distrust, while savedregs' answer is an English sentence that reads as a cleared axis.

MEASURED 2026-09-03 at commit 27ec16bcc on game/game/gamemain::DoWorldAnimation, a function carrying a copy_register_fields rule over 13 of its 63 instructions. `python tools/gdl/savedregs.py game/game/gamemain DoWorldAnimation` prints a six-row table in which every OURS cell equals its TARGET cell, followed by `ASSIGNMENT MATCHES: every callee-saved register holds the same value at its FIRST definition in both streams. That closes the first-definition assignment question and nothing else`. The SAME command with `--raw` prints `ROLE MISMATCH on 4 web(s)`, `LIFETIME PERMUTATION: 5 live range(s)`, and the four rows the residual actually consists of - `r31: target holds 'li 0', ours holds 'mr r3'` and its three siblings. Both runs are correct about the object they read; only one of them is about the compiler's output.

WHY THIS COSTS MORE THAN A RE-RUN. savedregs is the tool AGENTS.md nominates for exactly this residual class ('savedregs.py <unit> <fn> [--uses] # callee-saved correspondence, BOTH streams, zero builds'), and the class it is nominated for - callee-saved permutations - is heavily populated by pinned functions, because a clean callee-saved permutation is precisely what earns a copy_register_fields rule in the first place. So the default is wrong most often exactly where the tool is most useful. The `--raw` flag IS documented, in the module docstring's usage block ('savedregs.py <unit> <fn> --raw  # pre-webfrank body'), and that is not enough: nothing in the OUTPUT distinguishes a real all-clear from a pinned one, so a lane that never reads the docstring gets a confident false negative with no tell. This lane made that mistake on DoWorldAnimation and had to redo the correspondence.

THE RULE. On any function that `wf_word_diff` reports as `PINNED = YES`, pass `--raw` to savedregs, and quote the flag in any record that cites a savedregs verdict - a savedregs correspondence quoted without it is not evidence about a pinned function. The tool-side fix is one line of reporting rather than a behaviour change: print the same PIN SCREEN paragraph wf_word_diff prints, naming the rule and the flag, whenever the function is pinned and `--raw` was not passed. Changing the DEFAULT would be the wrong fix, because for the ~2589 unpinned STRICT functions the postprocessed object is the right one to read.
